exemplars.name: From a single file
exemplars.summary: A one-page artifact converted into a site that still looks the same: the original kept beside it, the conversion script, a tool that proves the page unchanged, and the site that came out.
exemplars.copyWhen: you already have a page — an AI artifact, an export, a hand-written HTML file — and want a site a web developer could take over.

exemplars.name: Blog
exemplars.summary: Posts as a fan-out, pagination, tag pages, an RSS feed, a rename kept alive with aliases, and every internal link written with {{link}}.
exemplars.copyWhen: the site has posts in it: a blog, a news section, a changelog.

exemplars.name: Data-fed site
exemplars.summary: A site built from a folder of records, each validated in its controller. One record is broken on purpose, so the build fails and says which.
exemplars.copyWhen: the content comes from data you don't control.

exemplars.name: Versioned outputs
exemplars.summary: One build per season into its own folder, published atomically, with an archive index beside them.
exemplars.copyWhen: you publish a new edition beside the old ones.

exemplars.name: Migrated from v1
exemplars.summary: Every v1 to v2 migration recipe as running code, in a site that builds clean and ships a recorded knowledge base.
exemplars.copyWhen: you're moving a v1 project across.

features.name: Scan
features.summary: .scan() registers every view in pages/, matching models and controllers by filename.

features.name: Page
features.summary: .page() four ways: matched, explicit, an object model with its own extension, and a template string.

features.name: Pages
features.summary: .pages() fans out one page per JSON file, and the index reuses the same array.

features.name: Layouts and partials
features.summary: One layout with blocks, nested .hbs, .html and .md partials, and a partial chosen at render time.

features.name: Helpers
features.summary: The built-in helpers on one page, plus custom dev-server ports.

features.name: Sitemap and llms.txt
features.summary: .sitemap() and .llms() with a siteUrl, per-page tuning, extension-less URLs and hashed assets.

features.name: Asset pipeline
features.summary: An external tool run before the asset copy, kept watching in dev mode, and the four shapes {{asset}} takes.
